name: 蔡銘修
objective: This course explores gamification and game-based learning in the AI era. In the first half, students use generative AI to design interactive gamified experiences; in the second, they develop and evaluate playable game-based learning experiences. The course emphasizes motivation, game mechanics, feedback, adaptation, and evaluation, with applications in education, workplace training, business, and other professional contexts.

materials:
Selected journal articles, case studies, and online resources related to gamification, game-based learning, and AI-enhanced learning will be provided through Google Classroom.

Students will also use generative AI and interactive development tools, such as ChatGPT, Gemini Canvas, Claude Artifacts, and other emerging tools, for idea generation, prototyping, game development, and evaluation.

Recommended references:

Kapp, K. M. (2012). The Gamification of Learning and Instruction. Pfeiffer.
Chou, Y. K. (2015). Actionable Gamification: Beyond Points, Badges, and Leaderboards. Octalysis Media.
Selected recent SSCI journal articles on gamification, game-based learning, serious games, and AI-enhanced learning.
